name: General Engineering
summary: A broad engineering degree that starts with heavy maths, physics and chemistry and then narrows into one of four specialisations: Living Systems, Advanced Materials, Cyber Systems or Future Energy. Year one introduces at least two of the specialisations through design-build projects, and the third year leaves room for a semester abroad or an industry project. About 60 per cent of the students are international, so it suits you if you want an engineering degree in English without having to pick your exact branch at 17.
